name: Confirm Placement Details
description: Agree tasks, dates, and hours with the studio; confirm your mentor and reporting line.
flavor: Clear expectations make great design possible.

name: Complete Design Onboarding
description: Set up design tools, access the game engine, and review the project's design bible.
flavor: Know the rules before you break them.

name: Design & Implement a Feature
description: Prototype and iterate on a gameplay mechanic, system, or level section.
flavor: Design is iteration made visible.

name: Log Design Hours & Reflection
description: Record hours and reflect on design decisions, playtest feedback, and iterations.
flavor: A design log is a portfolio in waiting.

name: Design Reflection
description: Write a reflection on your design process, challenges solved, and player impact.
flavor: Reflection turns iterations into evidence.

name: Feature Shipped
description: Your designed feature is in a playable build. Document the player-facing result.
flavor: Shipped design is the only design that matters.

name: Measure Design Impact
description: Explain how your design improved player engagement, retention, or clarity.
flavor: Data validates design.

name: Book Studio Visit
description: Arrange a visit to a game studio's design department. Confirm date, NDA, and agenda.
flavor: See how pros structure their design process.

name: Attend Design Review
description: Sit in on a design critique, playtest session, or systems walkthrough.
flavor: Watch how decisions get made at scale.

name: Find Game Jam Volunteer Role
description: Join a game jam or student project as a designer. Confirm scope and team needs.
flavor: Game jams are design bootcamps.

name: Design for a Game Jam
description: Create mechanics, levels, or systems for a 48-hour game jam project.
flavor: Constraints breed creativity.

name: Game Jam Feedback
description: Collect feedback from teammates and players on your design contributions.
flavor: Jam feedback is raw and honest.

name: Understand the Design Brief
description: Clarify the creative brief: core loop, target audience, platform constraints, and pillars.
flavor: A brief understood is half the battle won.

name: Deliver Design Documentation
description: Produce a design doc, flowcharts, or prototype for the brief. Iterate on feedback.
flavor: Docs are conversation starters, not contracts.

name: Document Design Learnings
description: Write a post-mortem on the brief: what worked, what changed, what you'd do differently.
flavor: Every brief teaches a new constraint.

name: Partner Design Review
description: Agree on design deliverables with an industry partner: mechanics, systems, or UX flows.
flavor: Partners want fresh eyes on old problems.

name: Complete Partner Design Task
description: Deliver a design prototype, system spec, or balance pass for the industry partner.
flavor: Professional feedback sharpens your instincts.

name: Showcase Partner Design
description: Present your partner work with context: brief, process, iteration, and outcome.
flavor: Show the thinking, not just the result.

name: Partner Design Adopted
description: Your design work influenced the partner's project direction or was implemented.
flavor: Real impact beats hypothetical every time.

name: Agree Dates & Schedule
description: Confirm the schedule and hours in writing. Must fit college hours (8:30am–5:30pm, max 8hr day).
flavor: Verbal agreements evaporate. Written ones stick.

name: Agree Your Design Role
description: Clarify design responsibilities: systems, levels, narrative, UI, or a mix.
flavor: Undefined design work is scope creep waiting to happen.

name: Design Mentor Contact
description: Get a named design mentor and a way to reach them — email, Slack, or LinkedIn.
flavor: A mentor's time is the best resource you'll have.

name: Find a Studio
description: Identify a studio whose games match your design interests and values.
flavor: Design for games you'd want to play.

name: Complete Design Assignment
description: Finish a course assignment demonstrating design thinking relevant to your target role.
flavor: Grades open doors. Design skills keep them open.

name: Iterate on Design Feedback
description: Improve a design using specific feedback. Shows growth mindset and adaptability.
flavor: First pass is for you. Second pass is for the player.

name: Ask for a Design Reference
description: Request written feedback from a design lead or mentor who supervised your work.
flavor: A reference is a vote of confidence in writing.

name: Write a Design CV Bullet
description: Describe your design contribution, the problem solved, and the player impact.
flavor: Don't list features. List player outcomes.

name: Daily Design Log
description: Record what you designed, what you tested, and what you learned each day.
flavor: Design unrecorded is design forgotten.

name: Design Distinction Earned
description: Bonus evidence: your design work was recognised for excellence.
flavor: Excellence isn't an accident. It's intentional design.

name: Save Design Portfolio Piece
description: Keep a finished design doc, prototype, or case study and explain your role and outcome.
flavor: Your portfolio is your proof. Make it undeniable.

name: Travel & Studio Access Plan
description: Check location, travel, hardware needs, and any studio access requirements.
flavor: The best plan fails if you can't get through the door.

name: Wild Card: Design Mentor
description: A design mentor guides your approach. Use in place of any Setup, Action, or Proof card for a Live Project Brief.
flavor: The best designers had mentors first.

name: Wild Card: Careers Team
description: Careers team connects you with a design placement. Use in place of any Setup, Action, or Proof card for a Block Placement.
flavor: They know which studios hire junior designers.

name: Wild Card: Portfolio Review
description: A portfolio review strengthens your evidence. Use in place of a Proof card for a Block Placement.
flavor: Fresh eyes see what you've missed.

name: Wild Card: Extended Iteration
description: Extra time to refine your design. Use in place of an Action card for a Live Project Brief.
flavor: Great design needs iteration time.

name: Wild Card: Tutor Design Review
description: A quick design check-in with your tutor. Use in place of a Setup card for Volunteering.
flavor: Sometimes the right question changes the design.
